title: Mongolian People's Republic
capsule: The Mongolian People's Republic, proclaimed on 26 November 1924 after Soviet-backed revolutionaries ousted the theocratic Bogd Khanate government, was the world's second communist state and remained a Soviet satellite until the democratic revolutions of 1990–1992. Under the long rule of Khorloogiin Choibalsan (1936–1952), the country endured Stalinist purges that killed tens of thousands, including nearly the entire Buddhist clergy. Economic integration with Comecon and collectivization of herding transformed Mongolian society, while the country served as a strategic buffer between the USSR and China. In 1990, mass protests forced the ruling party to accept multiparty elections; the republic was reconstituted as simply Mongolia under a new constitution adopted on 13 January 1992.
